verses.text: That day the Book of Moses was read aloud to the people. They found it written there that Ammonites and Moabites were never to enter God's assembly,
because they hadn't met the Israelites with bread and water, and instead hired Balaam to curse them. Our God turned the curse into a blessing.
When the people heard the law, they separated everyone of foreign descent from Israel.
Before this, Eliashib the priest, who was in charge of the storerooms in our God's house, had become an ally of Tobiah.

He had made a large room available to Tobiah where they used to store the grain offerings, incense, vessels, and tithes of grain, new wine, and oil required for the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, along with the offerings for the priests.
I was away from Jerusalem while this happened. In the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes, king of Babylon, I had gone back to the king. After a while I asked his permission to leave,
and when I returned to Jerusalem, I learned what a wrong Eliashib had done in giving Tobiah a room in the courtyards of God's house.
I was deeply upset, so I threw all Tobiah's belongings out of the room.
I ordered the rooms purified, then brought back the vessels of God's house, the grain offerings, and the incense.
I also found out that the Levites hadn't been given their shares. The Levites and singers who served had gone back to their fields.
I confronted the officials and asked, "Why has God's house been neglected?" Then I called the Levites and singers together and put them back at their posts.
All Judah brought the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil into the storerooms.

I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah the Levite in charge of the storerooms, with Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, as their assistant. They were considered trustworthy, and their job was to distribute the shares to their fellow workers.
My God, remember me for this. Don't erase the good I've done for your house and its worship.

In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath, gathering bundles of grain, and loading donkeys with wine, grapes, figs, and goods of every kind. They were bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. I warned them that day as they sold their food.
People from Tyre who lived there were also bringing in fish and all kinds of goods and selling them to the people of Judah in Jerusalem on the Sabbath.
I confronted Judah's nobles and said, "Why are you doing this evil thing and treating the Sabbath like any other day?
Didn't your ancestors do the same thing, and didn't our God bring all this disaster on us and this city? Now you're bringing more anger on Israel by profaning the Sabbath."

As darkness fell at Jerusalem's gates before the Sabbath, I ordered the doors shut and told them to keep them closed until the Sabbath was over. I stationed some of my men at the gates so no loads would be brought in on the Sabbath.
Once or twice the merchants and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.
I warned them, "Why are you camping by the wall? If you do it again, I'll have you seized." From then on they stopped coming on the Sabbath.
I told the Levites to purify themselves and come guard the gates to keep the Sabbath holy. My God, remember me for this too, and spare me in your great faithful love.
In those days I also saw Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Half their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and others spoke the languages of the other peoples. They didn't know how to speak the language of Judah.

I confronted them, cursed them, struck some of them, and pulled out their hair. I made them swear by God, "You must never give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters as wives for your sons or for yourselves.
Isn't this how King Solomon of Israel sinned? Among many nations there was no king like him. His God loved him and made him king over all Israel. Yet foreign women led even him into sin.
Are we supposed to hear that you've done this great wrong and been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women?"
One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, had married a daughter of Sanballat the Horonite, so I drove him away.
My God, remember them for defiling the priesthood and the covenant of the priests and Levites.
So I cleansed them of everything foreign and assigned the priests and Levites their duties, each to his own work.
I also arranged for the wood offerings at the appointed times and for the first produce. My God, remember me for good.
